request: why does a wind turbine make so much more power in stronger wind?

beats.intent: A turbine drawn as a tall pole with three blades, spinning
beats.narration: A wind turbine turns the push of moving air into electricity.
beats.code:
stage.title("Wind power")
pole = Line([0, -2.6, 0], [0, 0.8, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=8)
hub = Dot([0, 0.8, 0], radius=0.12, color=WHITE)
blades = VGroup(*[Line([0, 0.8, 0], [0, 0.8, 0] + 1.6 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
                  for a in (PI / 2, PI / 2 + TAU / 3, PI / 2 + 2 * TAU / 3)])
stage.play(Create(pole), Create(blades), FadeIn(hub))
stage.add(pole, blades, hub)
stage.play(Rotate(blades, -TAU, about_point=[0, 0.8, 0]), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)

beats.intent: Bars of power for wind speeds 1, 2 and 3 units: 1, 8, 27
beats.narration: Double the wind speed and the power goes up eight times; triple it and it goes up twenty seven times.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [1, 8, 27], labels=["speed 1", "speed 2", "speed 3"], color=TEAL)
stage.caption("power")

beats.narration: Faster air carries more energy in each bit of air, and more air arrives each second: that makes the power go as the cube of the speed.

request: how do you convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?

beats.intent: Axes of °C and °F with the line F = 1.8C + 32
beats.narration: Fahrenheit is a straight-line function of Celsius.
beats.code:
stage.title("Celsius to Fahrenheit")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-50, 110), y_range=(-60, 230), labels=("°C", "°F"))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda c: 1.8 * c + 32, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: Freezing (0, 32) and boiling (100, 212) marked on the line
beats.narration: Water freezes at zero Celsius, thirty two Fahrenheit, and boils at a hundred Celsius, two hundred and twelve Fahrenheit.
beats.code:
f = mark_point(stage, ax, (0, 32), color=BLUE, label="(0, 32)")
b = mark_point(stage, ax, (100, 212), color=RED, label="(100, 212)")

beats.intent: The line beside F = 1.8C + 32 and the point (-40, -40) where the scales agree
beats.narration: A hundred Celsius degrees span a hundred and eighty Fahrenheit ones, so multiply by one point eight and add thirty two. At minus forty, the two scales agree.
beats.code:
same = mark_point(stage, ax, (-40, -40), color=GREEN, label="(-40, -40)")
stage.equation(r"F = 1.8\,C + 32")

request: how many diagonals does a polygon have?

beats.intent: A pentagon with its 5 diagonals drawn, forming a star
beats.narration: A pentagon has five diagonals, and together they draw a star.
beats.code:
stage.title("Counting diagonals")
pent = RegularPolygon(5, color=BLUE).scale(1.6).move_to([-3.2, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(pent))
stage.add(pent)
V = pent.get_vertices()
d5 = [Line(V[i], V[j], color=YELLOW) for i in range(5) for j in range(i + 2, 5) if not (i == 0 and j == 4)]
stage.play(*[Create(l) for l in d5])
stage.add(*d5)
stage.label(pent, "5 diagonals", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

hexa = RegularPolygon(6, color=BLUE).scale(1.6).move_to([2.6, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(hexa))
stage.add(hexa)
W = hexa.get_vertices()
d6 = [Line(W[i], W[j], color=GREEN) for i in range(6) for j in range(i + 2, 6) if not (i == 0 and j == 5)]
stage.play(*[Create(l) for l in d6])
stage.add(*d6)
stage.label(hexa, "9 diagonals", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.narration: Each of the n corners joins to every corner except itself and its two neighbours: n minus three. Each diagonal is counted from both ends, so halve it.

request: how do contour lines on a map show a hill?

beats.intent: Nested loops around a hilltop, labelled 100, 200, 300 m
beats.narration: On a map, each contour line joins points at the same height: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred metres.
beats.code:
stage.title("Contour lines")
loops = VGroup()
for k, (w, h, dx) in enumerate(((6.0, 3.4, 0.0), (4.2, 2.4, 0.5), (2.4, 1.4, 0.9))):
    loops.add(Ellipse(width=w, height=h, color=[GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE][k]).move_to([-1.5 + dx, 0.6, 0]))
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(l) for l in loops], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(loops)
for l, t in zip(loops, ["100 m", "200 m", "300 m"]):
    stage.label(l, t, direction=UP, color=l.get_color())

beats.intent: The loops close together on the right side, far apart on the left
beats.narration: Where the lines bunch up, the ground climbs fast: a steep slope. Where they spread out, it is gentle.
beats.code:
steep = Arrow([1.2, 0.6, 0], [2.3, 0.6, 0], buff=0, color=RED)
gentle = Arrow([-2.2, 0.6, 0], [-4.5, 0.6, 0], buff=0, color=BLUE)
stage.play(GrowArrow(steep), GrowArrow(gentle))
stage.add(steep, gentle)
stage.label(steep, "steep", direction=DOWN, color=RED)
stage.label(gentle, "gentle", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: A side view of the hill below: a gentle slope on the left and a steep one on the right
beats.narration: Slice through the hill and you see it: a long gentle climb from the left, a steep drop on the right.
beats.code:
profile = VMobject(color=WHITE).set_points_smoothly([[-4.5, -3.2, 0], [-2.2, -2.7, 0], [-0.6, -2.2, 0], [0.3, -1.7, 0], [1.2, -2.3, 0], [2.3, -3.2, 0]])
ground = Line([-5, -3.2, 0], [3, -3.2, 0], color=GREY_B)
VGroup(ground, profile).shift(0.4 * UP)
stage.play(Create(ground), Create(profile))
stage.add(ground, profile)
stage.caption("side view: close lines, steep ground")
